transcript.text: Thank you all for being here. As you know, I've received Grandma's stained-glass window — it's 90 by 60 centimeters — and I want to get it displayed in the family home before our autumn gathering. We have three possible locations: the south-facing breakfast-room window, the west hallway, or the reading room. We can use a protective covering and either focused spotlights or a diffuse wall wash. And importantly, the window should remain available for family members to view without an appointment. Before I make any decisions, I'd like to do what I usually do: go around the table and hear from each of you. Please share what you know, what you need, or what you can commit to regarding this project. Who'd like to start?

transcript.text: I have something important to share on the conservation side. This would protect the window from UV damage and allow air circulation to prevent condensation buildup. I haven't had a chance to pass this along to the group until now.
